title: Understanding Teacher Perspectives and Experiences After Deployment of AI Literacy Curriculum in Middle-School Classrooms
extended_summary:
This paper examines how middle-school teachers experienced implementing modules from the MIT RAICA (Responsible AI for Computational Action) curriculum and how their beliefs about AI and teaching evolved through the process. The study is motivated by a gap in AI education research: much prior work has centered researchers as instructors, leaving limited evidence from classroom teachers about what supports are needed for successful implementation of AI literacy curricula.

The intervention consisted of three project-based AI literacy modules deployed in middle-school classrooms. Teachers received ongoing professional development, interacted with RAICA researchers during weekly debrief sessions, and then participated in semi-structured interviews after implementation. Seven teachers from interdisciplinary backgrounds (art, business, and computer science) were interviewed about how they adapted the modules, their attitudes toward AI before/during/after implementation, and their perceptions of the curriculum and support resources. The classroom modules included activities such as building an interactive art installation, creating a chatbot, or designing an app for the school community.

Findings show that the curriculum expanded teachers’ AI knowledge, increased attention to ethical and societal implications of AI, and encouraged teachers to draw on their own interdisciplinary strengths to engage students. Teachers valued the flexibility of the curriculum but also reported needing more technical support, clearer guidance, more time for preparation, and better accommodations for diverse learners. Overall, the paper concludes that AI literacy curricula for middle school are more effective when paired with sustained teacher support, concrete scaffolding, and opportunities for continuous feedback during development and early deployment.

identified_tools.name: CAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Computer-assisted instruction / AI-enabled curriculum or educational software used to support teaching and learning.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper studies teacher experiences implementing the MIT RAICA AI literacy curriculum in middle-school classrooms, including teacher professional development and classroom deployment of curriculum modules.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers reported that the RAICA curriculum expanded their knowledge of AI concepts, helped them recognize AI's daily applications and ethical implications, and supported more confident adaptation of lessons to their classrooms. They also described increased appreciation for peer support and the curriculum's flexibility, but requested more scaffolding, technical support, and one-on-one code review during PD.
findings.measure: Teacher interview themes on AI knowledge growth, confidence, adaptation of curriculum materials, and implementation challenges

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/mixed-methods study based on semi-structured interviews with seven teachers, not an experimental evaluation. It provides useful implementation insight but no causal evidence or quantitative effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports positive perceived impact on teacher knowledge and confidence, but impact is not quantified and is based on self-reported experiences. Any effect on uptake or practice is suggestive rather than measured with robust outcome data.
